thread:
Alex: Heads up — planning a tiny traffic tilt for eu-north tonight during the quiet window. Start 01:30 UTC, expected ~15–25m. Goal: move ~6% baseline from eu-legacy to eu-new-edge for perf testing and shorten DNS TTL to 600s for quick rollback.
Mira: Sounds good. Which services and are there any schema or feature flag changes? :thinking_face:
Alex: Config-only. In-scope: generation-api (read), embeddings, auth-proxy. No schema changes, no feature flags toggled. We're only adjusting route weights + DNS TTL.
Jonas: Who's owning the change and who’s on rollback? I can take primary if needed.
Alex: Jonas primary, Casey backup. Eng-platform oncall will monitor. I'll post the route patch and DNS update. deploy-bot: scheduling now.
deploy-bot: Job created: region-tilt-eun-2026-01-30 01:30 UTC. Job ID: rb-8142. Auto-rollback policy: error rate +4% over 3m or 95p latency +10% over baseline.
eng-platform-oncall: I'll attach the temporary alert hooks and watch traces. Quick checklist I'm running:
- pre: curl -fsS https://eun.api.redwood.internal/health | jq -r .status (expect "ok")
- pre: kubectl get deploy generation-api -n prod-eu-north -o wide
- during: POST /v1/generate with header x-e2e-test:1 and small prompt
- post: check 95p latency on telemetry and token error counts in logs
Mira: DNS plan confirmed: change TTL 1800 -> 600 at t0, revert to 1800 after 45m of stability.
Alex: Exact weights: current eu-legacy 74%, eu-new-edge 26% => target eu-legacy 68%, eu-new-edge 32% (+6%). Patch snippet for route-control: ```PATCH /route-control/v1/policies/eu-north { "buckets": [{"id":"eu-legacy","weight":68},{"id":"eu-new-edge","weight":32}] }```
Jonas: Copy. I'll apply route patch and then update TTL via route-control DNS API. What's the revert payload if we need to roll back?
Casey: Revert = previous payload job-rb-8100 saved, TTL back to 1800. Quick rollback steps I have:
1) apply payload job-rb-8100 to route-control (restore weights),
2) set DNS TTL=1800,
3) scale generation-api to previous replica target if error% spikes: kubectl scale deploy generation-api --replicas=12 -n prod-eu-north,
4) if still bad after 10m, page eng-platform escalation.
eng-platform-oncall: I'll raise trace sample rate and tag traces with meta=rb-8142 for 30m. Also will add a temporary dashboard with token error and 95p latency.
deploy-bot: Reminder pings scheduled at 01:05 UTC and 01:20 UTC.
Jonas: Preflight done at 01:20: health ok, pods 8/8, ready, no in-progress rollouts. I'll be at keyboard 01:10–01:40 UTC.
Mira: Running smoke at 01:35: generate ok, 95p latency 240ms (baseline 230ms), no 5xx. Trace: https://observability.redwood/trace/zz-eun-456
Alex: Good. Proceeding to apply route weights + TTL.
(deploy actions logged)
Jonas: Route-control returned 200 for patch, TTL set to 600.
eng-platform-oncall: Monitoring: errors steady, 95p latency +7ms, KV cache hit rate unchanged. No alerts triggered.
Mira: Smoke tests at 01:40 — all green, samples look normal.
Casey: Still watching for any amplification in embeddings calls; we had a small tail last week.
Alex: We'll keep the window open for 45m. If stable at ~02:15 UTC I'll flip TTL back to 1800.
Jonas: I'll stay reachable for the next 30m. Ping me for any anomaly. :white_check_mark:
eng-platform-oncall: Noted. Closing temporary hooks at 02:20 if everything remains quiet.
Alex: Thanks all. I'll post a brief postmortem note in the morning with metrics and any lessons learned.
